title: Interfaces vs Abstract Classes in Java

scenes.say: Ever wonder when to use an interface versus an abstract class in Java?
Interfaces set the rules but can't hold data. Abstract classes can store state and share code. Since Java eight, interfaces can also have default methods with logic.
Here's a Shape interface. It has an area method and a default print method. Default methods let you add logic to interfaces without breaking old code.

scenes.label: Choice
scenes.sub: Use interfaces for contracts, abstract classes for shared state.
scenes.say: My rule: interfaces for contracts and reusable logic, abstract classes when I need to store fields.

scenes.question: Can interfaces have fields?
scenes.right: No, interfaces can't have instance fields—only constants.
scenes.say: Watch out: interfaces can't have instance fields. Only constants are allowed.
